QF.id: Cat III AIF Fees and Performance_27

question.text: A Cat III AIF's incentive fees payable MUST align interests of the Manager with the Fund. Which mechanism BEST achieves this?

answer.text: Paying incentive fees upfront at commitment
Combining Hurdle rate AND High-Water Mark in the fee computation

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that incentive fees are meant to align the manager's interest with the fund and introduces the High-Water Mark to safeguard investors. Example 3 applies the higher of HWM and reference hurdle when testing incentive-fee eligibility, so using both the hurdle rate and HWM ensures the investor's preferred return and NAV-value creation are checked before incentive fees are paid. The Trap: Upfront incentive fees, an arbitrary 50% rate, or removing incentive fees altogether do not meet the workbook's hurdle-plus-HWM alignment standard. Note: Per workbook pages 168 and 173-175.
